value.rationale: A 2026 network-game convergence study directly motivates exact rather than epsilon-defined time-to-equilibrium on canonical high-degree stars. The finding classifies every star size and every strength, identifies a sharp degree-four one-sweep onset, separates the known equilibrium threshold from an exact transient first-zero invariant, and proves symmetric two-sided logarithmic critical slowdowns. The finite-word random absorption result and first-pass deactivation probability connect this structural dynamical classification to randomized scheduling. These are natural parameters and are not an arbitrary finite sample or mere recomputation of a known equilibrium table.
